item: Document every table and column the agent may access including sensitivity classification and owning team
rationale: Agents cannot infer data sensitivity or ownership from schema names alone

item: Define business-vocabulary mappings for every concept the agent will be asked about
rationale: Raw schemas use implementation names; agents need a common business vocabulary to select the correct tables

item: Specify which roles or individuals are authorized to see each semantic entity and enforce this at query time
rationale: Describing authorization in metadata does not prevent the agent from returning restricted data to unauthorized users
Agents should not operate with union permissions that let them bypass row-level or column-level security

item: Time-bound agent access and require re-authorization after a defined period
rationale: Persistent credentials enable long-lived exposure if an agent is compromised or misconfigured

item: Log every query the agent generates including requesting user timestamp semantic intent and SQL executed
rationale: Without logs you cannot diagnose over-permissioned queries or trace data exfiltration after the fact

item: Test the agent against realistic ambiguous or adversarial questions
rationale: Benign test queries will not surface the agent's behavior when a user requests restricted information

item: Establish a rollback procedure to revoke agent access within one business day
rationale: You must be able to disable the agent without disrupting core operations

item: Validate every agent-generated query against a known-good query catalog before execution
rationale: Structural validation can catch malformed or suspicious queries that bypass semantic-layer guardrails

item: Filter agent output to remove any column not explicitly declared in the semantic layer
rationale: Agents may select columns outside the intended business vocabulary if schema introspection is allowed

item: Rate-limit agent queries per user and per session
rationale: High-frequency queries may indicate automated data extraction rather than interactive analysis

item: Review agent query logs weekly with a data steward
rationale: Emergent misuse or confusion often appears in aggregate patterns not in any single query

item: Document every business metric the agent is expected to surface and validate its query logic
rationale: Divergence between agent-reported metrics and dashboard metrics erodes trust

item: Require governance review before adding new tables or columns to the semantic layer
rationale: Expanding the vocabulary also expands the attack surface

item: Test the agent's behavior when a user asks a question spanning multiple permission boundaries
rationale: Cross-boundary queries are a common failure mode; the agent must deny or redact properly

item: Define an incident-response playbook for scenarios where the agent returns unauthorized data
rationale: Detection is only useful if your team knows who to notify and how to contain the exposure

item: Maintain a contact list of data owners for every table in the semantic layer
rationale: Data owners are often the first to recognize when usage does not match legitimate business activity
